title: Advice on Successfully Keeping New Year’s Promises
speaker: VOA Learning English

sentences.en: From VOA Learning English, this is the Health & Lifestyle Report .
sentences.zh: 《健康与生活方式报告》。

sentences.en: As the new year begins, some people see an opportunity for change and improvement.
sentences.zh: 随着新年的开始,一些人看到变革和改善的机会。

sentences.en: Experts say January can be a good time to think about self-improvement.
sentences.zh: 专家说一月是思考自我改善的好时机。

sentences.en: Many people make resolutions. But these promises we make to ourselves require effort to become part of our daily lives.
sentences.zh: 许多人作出了决议,但是,我们对自己作出的这些保证需要努力才能成为我们日常生活的一部分。

sentences.en: They are meant to last a long time. Studies have shown that up to 70 percent of people who make New Year’s resolutions quit their plans within months.
sentences.zh: 研究显示,高达70%的通过新年决议的人在几个月内就放弃了计划。

sentences.en: Recently, experts gave advice on keeping New Year's resolutions to the Associated Press.
sentences.zh: 最近,专家们向美联社提出了关于保持新年决议的建议。

sentences.en: Start small It is difficult to make big changes.
sentences.zh: 从小开始,很难做出重大改变。

sentences.en: Behavioral health experts suggest breaking big goals into smaller targets.
sentences.zh: 行为卫生专家建议把大目标变成小目标。

sentences.en: For example, if your goal is to improve your health, you could start with small changes.
sentences.zh: 例如,如果你的目标是改善你的健康,你可以从小的变化开始。

sentences.en: For some meals, you could trade unhealthy foods for healthy ones, or you could exercise for 10 minutes each day.
sentences.zh: 对于一些食物,你可以用不健康的食物换健康的食物, 或者你可以每天锻炼10分钟。

sentences.en: Once you start reaching smaller goals, the bigger one might not seem so daunting .
sentences.zh: 一旦你开始 达到较小的目标, 更大的可能看起来不那么令人生畏。

sentences.en: Be realistic Psychologist Lynn Bufka suggests being realistic about resolutions.
sentences.zh: 现实的心理学家林恩·布夫卡建议对决议持现实态度。

sentences.en: She is with the American Psychological Association based in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 她是美国心理协会的会员,总部设在华盛顿特区。

sentences.en: “It’s quite daunting to say that you want to lose 50 pounds and thus, will never eat dessert again,” she said. “It might be more helpful to say, you’re only going to have dessert on the weekends and for special occasions .”
sentences.zh: ”她说 : “ 说你想减掉50磅,再也不会吃甜点,这非常令人生畏。 ” “也许更有用的是说,你只在周末和特殊场合吃甜点。 ”

sentences.en: Mindset change Think about what your resolution is helping you to achieve .
sentences.zh: 想想你的解决方案能帮助你实现什么。

sentences.en: Do not think about what you are giving up.
sentences.zh: 别想着要放弃什么

sentences.en: This can be a powerful way to change your mindset.
sentences.zh: 这会是改变你心态的有力方法

sentences.en: Bufka said that thinking positively about your end goal and the benefits of your changed behavior can increase your motivation, or drive to succeed.
sentences.zh: 布夫卡说,积极思考你的终极目标 以及你改变行为的好处 可以提高你的动机,或推动成功。

sentences.en: Bufka gave this example. “If I put money in a jar for what I would have spent on chocolate every day, that starts to add up,” she explained.
sentences.zh: 布夫卡举了这个例子。 她解释说,“如果我把钱放进罐子里,为了我每天花在巧克力上的钱,这开始加起来。

sentences.en: Make specific goals A study of New Year’s resolutions published in 2020 found that people who pay attention to specific goals are more successful than those simply trying to give up bad habits .
sentences.zh: 对2020年发表的新年决议的研究发现,关注具体目标的人比那些试图放弃不良习惯的人更成功。

sentences.en: In a group of more than 1,000 people, scientists found the most popular resolutions involved exercise, weight loss and eating habits.
sentences.zh: 在1 000多人中,科学家发现最受欢迎的解决办法涉及锻炼、减肥和饮食习惯。

sentences.en: Other resolutions had to do with self-improvement, personal finance, and ways to take care of mental health and to reduce stress .
sentences.zh: 其他决议涉及自我改善、个人资金以及照顾精神健康和减轻压力的方法。

sentences.en: Among the 55 percent of people who said they had kept their resolutions after one year, nearly 60 percent of them had made resolutions involving goals.
sentences.zh: 55%的人说他们在一年后保留了自己的决议,其中近60%的人提出了涉及目标的决议。

sentences.en: This is compared with 47 percent who chose to avoid behaviors.
sentences.zh: 相比之下,选择避免行为的占47%。

sentences.en: Involve other people Involving others in your efforts might also help.
sentences.zh: 让其他人参与你的努力也会有所帮助。

sentences.en: Other people can offer support and hold you accountable .
sentences.zh: 其他人可以提供支持 并追究你的责任。

sentences.en: When we are held accountable, we are responsible for our actions.
sentences.zh: 当我们被追究责任时,我们应对我们的行动负责。

sentences.en: Someone who decides to start exercising more, for example, might join a running group or sign up for a gym class with friends.
sentences.zh: 例如,一个决定开始锻炼的人, 可能会加入一个运行的团体,或者报名参加一个有朋友的体育课。

sentences.en: This can also make exercising more fun. Use technology Experts also suggest using planners to help you keep your resolutions.
sentences.zh: 使用技术专家也建议使用规划者来帮助您保存您的解决方案 。

sentences.en: For example, you can plan your activities for a specific period every morning or evening.
sentences.zh: 例如,您可以每天早上或晚上为特定时间计划活动。

sentences.en: Use reminders and timers on your smartphone.
sentences.zh: 在你的智能手机上使用提醒和计时器。

sentences.en: And use group texts for group activities.
sentences.zh: 使用分组文本进行分组活动。

sentences.en: Be kind to yourself Changing our behavior is difficult, so do not expect perfection .
sentences.zh: 改变我们的行为是困难的, 所以不要期望完美。

sentences.en: There will be times when it feels impossible to keep your resolution, and you will want to give up.
sentences.zh: 有时你无法坚持自己的决心 你会想放弃的

sentences.en: “A great resolution might be, ‘I will be less judgmental with myself,’” said Tamara Russell of the British Psychological Society. “Research shows that the more we develop self- compassion , the more compassionate we can become towards others.”
sentences.zh: 英国心理学会的Tamara Russell说 : “ 伟大的解决方案可能是,`我会对自己少点判断力'。 ” “研究显示,我们自我同情越多,对他人的同情就越多。 ”

sentences.en: Review and make changes To better keep resolutions, Russell suggests reviewing each week.
sentences.zh: 为了更好地保持决议,罗素建议每周审查一次。

sentences.en: Ask yourself: what has worked? What has not?
sentences.zh: 问问你自己:什么奏效了?什么没有?

sentences.en: She said, “Study your own behavior like a scientist.” Russell added that we should not be afraid to change our resolutions.
sentences.zh: 她说,“像科学家一样研究你自己的行为。 ”罗素补充说,我们不应该害怕改变我们的决议。

sentences.en: Choose the right time The last piece of advice might be the most important.
sentences.zh: 选择正确的时间 最后一个建议可能是最重要的

sentences.en: If January 1 feels like a bad time to create a new resolution, make the changes when it makes sense for you.
sentences.zh: 如果1月1日觉得不是时候 来制定新的决议, 当它让你有意义的时候, 做出改变。

sentences.en: Russell said it makes “no sense at all” to make resolutions connected to the calendar year.
sentences.zh: Russell说,把决议与日历年联系起来“完全没有意义”。

sentences.en: Winter is usually a time of rest for much of the natural world.
sentences.zh: 冬天通常是自然界大部分地方的休息时间。

sentences.en: She said that spring is the season of growth and renewal.
sentences.zh: 她说,春天是成长和复兴的季节。

sentences.en: So, depending on your life’s situation, spring might be a better time for most people to make changes.
sentences.zh: 因此,根据你的生活状况,春天或许是大多数人进行变革的好时机。

sentences.en: And that’s the Health & Lifestyle Report .
sentences.zh: 这是《健康与生活方式报告》。

sentences.en: I’m Anna Matteo. Maria Cheng reported this story for The Associated Press from New York City.
sentences.zh: 我是Anna Matteo, Maria Cheng在纽约市为美联社报导此事。

sentences.en: Anna Matteo adapted it for VOA Learning English.
sentences.zh: Anna Matteo改编成VOA英文学习版。
